In an effort to get more than a merely peppery ginger beer soda, I have been altering my simple recipe with more ginger and also blending it instead of slicing, and, of course, simmering longer.

This did help increase the heat a bit, and made for more body to the soda, making it less like soda water and more like ginger. The 1/8th tsp dab of molasses I used to feed the yeast may have helped, certainly it gave the drink a warm yellow colour.

After drinking it a few times, though, I noticed that the heat was more intense if the sediment (increased, because of the blending) was stirred up compared to the first pour from a settled bottle. I was getting more heat, but the extraction process wasn't very efficient.

One batch I used about 2-3 tsp of molasses, but it was far too much. Half of that might taste better. The molasses was far too obvious a flavour.

So back to the extraction process. I either need to try the simmer with a better solvent (alcohol) or try the altogether different approach, a ginger bug. Starting a bug has been in the back of my mind for some time now, but always I put it off. Maybe it's time...
Oops, the title is in reference to the molasses heavy batch.
